records.title: SHANK3 drives abnormal neurodevelopment in iPSC-derived 2D and 3D brain models of Phelan-McDermid Syndrome.
records.abstract: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome (PMDS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by 22q13.3 deletion involving SHANK3. While SHANK3 is critical for synapses, its role in early human neurodevelopment remains elusive. Here, we generated induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived 2D neuronal cultures and 3D cerebral organoids from two twin Phelan-McDermid syndrome patients with a 1.7 Mb 22q13 deletion encompassing SHANK3 gene. PMDS organoids showed reduced volume due to impaired neural progenitor cells (NPCs) proliferation. PMDS NPCs exhibited biased differentiation with decreased excitatory neurons but increased GFAP+ astroglia and GABAergic neurons. PMDS neurons displayed simplified morphology, reduced synapse density and diminished excitability. Importantly, lentiviral-mediated SHANK3 overexpression largely rescued these defects. Our findings identify SHANK3 as a key regulator of early neurodevelopment and provide mechanistic insights into PMDS pathogenesis.

records.title: Epidermal Differentiation Disorders (EDDs): Translational insights and technical challenges of three-dimensional epidermal, full-thickness, and organoid skin models.
records.abstract: Monogenic epidermal differentiation disorders (EDDs) are individually rare, but collectively affect many patients, often causing lifelong morbidity. Recent advances in genetics prompted the Reclassifying Epidermal Differentiation Disorders Initiative (REDDI) to introduce a gene-based classification of EDDs, replacing eponyms and grouping disorders as syndromic (sEDD), nonsyndromic (nEDD), or palmoplantar (pEDD). Because EDD pathology is largely epidermal and most disorders result from single gene variants, they are well suited for modelling in human keratinocytes grown within three-dimensional tissue models that can reproduce tissue-level pathology. We review published human epidermal equivalents (HEEs), skin equivalents (HSEs), epidermal organoids (HEOs), and skin organoids (HSOs) engineered to study EDDs. Most models replicated key disease features, including defective epidermal differentiation, tissue architecture, cell adhesion, and barrier function and provide platforms to investigate pathophysiology and evaluate therapeutic strategies. Most published models represent nEDDs, whereas pEDDs and sEDDs remain underrepresented due to disease features extending beyond the epidermis. Emerging bioengineering approaches, including incorporating additional cell types and application of extrinsic physical cues may help address these limitations. We also outline strategies for collaboration, resource sharing, advocacy, and targeted funding, which are essential to expand the repertoire of EDD models and accelerate development of effective therapies for these orphan disorders.

records.title: Spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia in the progression of gastric precancerous lesions: mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities-a narrative review.
records.abstract: Spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM) represents a gastric metaplastic phenotype situated at the intersection of mucosal repair and preneoplastic remodeling. While transient SPEM may facilitate epithelial restitution following acute injury, persistent SPEM in chronic inflammatory contexts correlates with incomplete intestinal metaplasia (IM), dysplastic epithelial states, and gastric carcinogenesis. This narrative review summarizes the biological characteristics and proposed cellular origins of SPEM. It critically examines the mechanisms governing SPEM initiation, persistence, and progression-associated remodeling. It also evaluates the evidence linking SPEM to incomplete IM and gastric carcinogenesis and discusses emerging therapeutic vulnerabilities and their translational limitations. PubMed and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from January 1, 2000 to April 30, 2026. Reference lists of relevant studies and guidelines were also screened. Human, animal, organoid, and other experimental studies with direct mechanistic or clinical relevance were included. The cellular origin of SPEM is model dependent. Acute models support chief-cell plasticity, whereas trefoil factor 2-expressing isthmal progenitors contribute in specific contexts. Single-cell analyses suggest convergence of mucous neck cells and chief-cell states without proving lineage conversion. SPEM involves disrupted epithelial homeostasis and paligenosis, together with growth factor, Wnt/β-catenin, and oncogenic signaling. Chronic Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori)injury, immune and stromal signals, and redox adaptation promote persistence. Human studies associate SPEM mainly with incomplete IM but do not establish obligatory progression to IM or cancer. H. pylori eradication remains the only recognized upstream intervention; SPEM-directed strategies remain preclinical. SPEM is a context-dependent reparative lineage whose association with preneoplastic remodeling is strongest in chronic injury. Human evidence links persistent SPEM to incomplete IM and dysplasia-associated states but does not establish an obligatory SPEM-to-IM-to-cancer sequence. Future progress requires distinguishing transient reparative SPEM from persistent, progression-associated SPEM, standardizing phenotypic criteria, conducting longitudinal human studies, and identifying targets that suppress pathological SPEM without impairing mucosal repair.

records.title: Controlled activin A signaling enables liver organoid generation from human pluripotent stem cells.
records.abstract: Morphogen gradients critically regulate the coordinated emergence of endodermal and mesodermal lineages during liver bud formation, yet current human hepatic organoid models inadequately replicate these spatial cues. Here, we examine how modulation of activin A signaling within a 3D vertical-wheel bioreactor culture system shapes early morphogenetic organization in human pluripotent stem cell aggregates. We observe that defined activin A conditions promote the spatial organization of human pluripotent stem cells during hepatic differentiation. High activin levels induce uniform definitive endoderm and enhanced hepatic competence, whereas low levels support the emergence of epithelial tube-like structures encased by mesenchymal cells, recapitulating early liver bud-like architecture. By leveraging differential activin A concentrations, this approach modulates the balance between morphogenesis and hepatic maturation in vertical-wheel-derived liver organoids, providing a scalable platform to model human liver organogenesis and engineer ventral foregut-derived tissues.

records.title: Towards regulatory acceptance of 3D in vitro mucosal models in non-clinical vaccine development and market authorization.
records.abstract: The Inno4Vac project aims to develop human 3D in vitro models to accelerate vaccine development. This study explores the integration potential of respiratory 3D in vitro models (air-liquid interface, lung-on-chip, and airway organoids) as predictive tools for non-clinical vaccine development and market authorisation, emphasising respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Being only semi-permissive for RSV, current animal models for RSV vaccines inadequately recapitulate human RSV pathogenesis allowing limited virus replication and virus-induced pathology. This limits the predictive value for safety and efficacy in humans, highlighting the need for alternative approaches. The recent approval of RSV vaccines (Arexvy®, Abrysvo®, and mResvia®) provides a timely regulatory framework for defining New Approach Methodologies (NAM) requirements. World Health Organisation guidelines, regulatory documentation (European Public Assessment Reports, Marketing Authorisation Applications), and published experimental data on respiratory 3D NAMs were reviewed. Where RSV-specific data were lacking, influenza infection models were evaluated. All NAMs recapitulated key human airway epithelium features and supported productive RSV and influenza infection, including viral replication, cytokine responses, and histopathological changes. Infection could be neutralized by monoclonal antibodies and immune serum from vaccinated donors. Incorporated immune components enhanced physiological relevance. Vaccine-enhanced respiratory disease from formalin-inactivated RSV could potentially be modelled through incorporation of immune components. Although these NAMs lack the adaptive immune system and cannot entirely replace animal immunogenicity studies, they contribute to non-clinical vaccine development as platforms for viral challenge, antibody neutralisation, innate immune profiling, and animal-to-human bridging. These advances directly support 3Rs principles, particularly for RSV, where animal models have limited predictive value.

records.title: Establishment of canine nasal carcinoma organoids for drug sensitivity testing and functional characterization of S100A2.
records.abstract: Canine nasal carcinoma (NC) is highly malignant and progressive, with metastasis. Radiation therapy is a common treatment; however, it has various drawbacks, including cost and anesthetic risks in elderly patients. Therefore, the development of alternative anti-cancer drug therapies has been required. In this study, we established an NC organoid culture method as an experimental model and explored more effective therapeutic targets. NC organoids were generated from patient-derived tissues from diseased dogs with NC. Electron microscopy of NC organoids revealed goblet cell differentiation with mucus granules and luminal structures. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CK19, E-cadherin, and Ki67, and their expression patterns corresponded to those in the original tissues. Furthermore, NC organoids were tumorigenic in immunodeficient mice. We identified useful supplements for culturing NC organoids and found that each NC organoid line exhibited different sensitivities to anti-cancer drugs. RNA sequencing was performed using samples from healthy dogs and NC organoids. Pathways related to MYC targets, oxidative phosphorylation, and protein secretion were enriched in NC organoids compared with normal nasal cells. Among the differentially expressed genes, S100A2 was selected for further functional investigation based on its increased expression and previously reported involvement in cancer-related processes. S100A2 knockdown reduced cell proliferation and invasiveness, supporting a functional contribution of S100A2 to malignant phenotypes in canine NC. These findings establish canine NC organoids as an experimental platform for investigating canine NC biology and provide a basis for future comparative studies.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Protein Design with Toolset Harnessing.
records.abstract: Computational protein design workflows require the orchestration of multiple tools, data formats, and analysis steps that are often fragmented. Here, we introduce Chaperone, a lightweight and customizable framework that enables seamless integration of RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) [1] with downstream sequence design, structure prediction, and evaluation tools, including ProteinMPNN [2], AlphaFold3 (AF3) [3], and more than 50 other protein design tools. By combining a programmable agent-friendly interface with parallelized execution on high-performance computing systems, Chaperone as a harness enables rapid iteration and scalable exploration of complex protein design workflows. Across an evaluation of nine biomolecular design tasks, we find using Chaperone reduces total token usage relative to baseline agents by 86% and GPU costs by 64%, while increasing the overall computational design pass rate. We demonstrate Chaperone's utility for large-scale design-space exploration through a two-week end-to-end small-molecule binder design campaign, yielding low nanomolar binders to cortisol zero shot. We further demonstrate its versatility across distinct design challenges, including the design of a symmetric 12-subunit self-assembly nanoparticle and a linker that mediates interactions between C2- and D3-symmetric protein complexes to form crystalline assemblies. Together, these results demonstrate how agent harnesses built around standardized tool interfaces can substantially improve the efficiency and success of complex, long-horizon agentic design workflows in biology. We make Chaperone freely available to the community on GitHub: https://github.com/RosettaCommons/chaperone .

records.title: MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth.
records.abstract: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. Here we design proteins that bind epitopes within regions of MYC whose sequence is conserved between human and mouse, including intrinsically disordered motifs required for oncogenic activity. In vitro, the designs bind MYC with nanomolar affinity and in cells they engage MYC, disrupt interactions with MAX, and remodel MYC-associated protein complexes. Expression of the binders decreases cell proliferation across diverse MYC-dependent hematopoietic, liver, pancreatic, and patient-derived tumor models, and in an orthotopic pancreatic cancer model, binder-expressing tumor cells were selectively depleted. This work establishes de novo protein design as a generalizable strategy to therapeutically target intrinsically disordered transcription factors. We developed a panel of de novo designed intracellular protein binders that target conserved functional regions of MYC with nanomolar affinity, remodel MYC complexes and interaction networks in cells, suppress proliferation across MYC-dependent cancer models, and are depleted from orthotopic pancreatic tumors in vivo.

records.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
records.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disordered regions. Advances in AI-driven protein design have recently opened new avenues for the rational development of molecules aimed at modulating these chromatin interactions. In this research, we implemented an integrated computational and experimental framework to design and validate peptides targeting the nucleosome acidic patch. We relied on the AI protein design approach implemented in BindCraft to design nucleosome binding peptides. To achieve precise quantitative analysis of these interactions, we refined a donor FRET quenching assay specifically for this application, enabling sensitive and consistent measurement of binding affinities for the designed sequences. We successfully identified peptides with high affinity for the acidic patch on canonical nucleosome core particles. These findings highlight the potential of AI-assisted design for chromatin-targeting agents and establish an effective workflow for their validation, laying the groundwork for synthetic epigenetic modulators and the broader use of protein design in managing 3D genome organization.

records.title: HydroGuard: a controlled release hydrogel-phage delivery system to combat catheter-associated urinary tract infections.
records.abstract: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) rank as the fourth-most significant nosocomial infection globally. CAUTIs account for approximately 80% of hospital-acquired urinary tract infections and represent nearly one-third of all device-associated infections. Urinary catheters serve as a hub for bacteria to form highly resistant biofilms containing pathogens, like Enterococcus (E.) faecalis that reduce effectiveness of the immune system and antibiotic treatments. Therefore, tackling biofilm formation at the catheter surface becomes a crucial step in mitigating CAUTIs. We aim to address E. faecalis biofilm formation by engineering HydroGuard: a Gelatin Methacryloyl (Gel-MA)-based hydrogel injected with bacteriophages, to provide targeted, enzyme-triggered antimicrobial activity. Enterococcus faecalis expresses gelatinase (GelE), a zinc metalloprotease that enhances biofilm formation. GelMA is susceptible to GelE-mediated degradation, enabling enzyme-triggered release of bacteriophages that specifically lyse E. faecalis. For a Biosafety Level 1 proof-of-concept experiment with a well-studied host and phage system, we heterologously expressed GelE in Escherichia (E.) coli DH5α to emulate native E. faecalis expression. This system was tested on dynamically grown biofilms, to simulate similar conditions to the urinary tract. Currently, the E. coli system has shown preliminary inhibition when tested against the hydrogel product, however testing of different phage combinations is needed. Mathematical modelling identified hydrogel crosslinking density as a critical tuneable parameter governing therapeutic availability and predicted nonlinear, degradation-dependent phage release profiles. Sensitivity analyses revealed design trade-offs between structural stability and antimicrobial responsiveness. Together, the biofilm, hydrogel, phage-bacteria, and protein design models form a multiscale computational framework that links biofilm development and environmental conditions to enzyme-mediated hydrogel degradation, phage release, and bacterial suppression. Agent-based biofilm simulations captured emergent spatial dynamics under nutrient, flow, and pH constraints, while a coupled predator-prey model investigated phage-bacteria population dynamics within the degrading GelMA matrix. Computational protein design further explored collagen-like peptide motifs with enhanced folding stability and preserved gelatinase cleavage sites, providing a molecular-level approach to tuneable degradation kinetics. This multiscale framework provides predictive insight into how biofilm conditions, hydrogel degradation, and phage availability interact within the proposed system, while the preliminary experimental observations provide supporting evidence for its feasibility. By integrating synthetic biology, tissue engineering, and modelling, HydroGuard offers a novel, non-antibiotic strategy for CAUTI prevention.

records.title: Function-preserving CD8+ T Cell Immunogenicity minimization through protein design.
records.abstract: Rapid advances in protein design enable new approaches in adoptive cell therapy, but foreign proteins can elicit cytotoxic T cell responses, and hence there is considerable need for approaches which reduce immunogenicity without compromising protein function. Here, we develop a computational framework integrating structure-guided sequence design with MHC class I epitope prediction to efficiently tune protein immunogenicity while preserving function. Using a de novo-designed luciferase as a model, we demonstrate epitope elimination while preserving function across 5 common mouse alleles and extend our computational optimization to 25 common human MHC-I alleles. In mice immunized with mRNA-lipid nanoparticles, variants designed to have few MHC-I epitopes elicited little detectable CD8+ T cell response, whereas variants designed to include multiple epitopes induced robust responses. Together, these results demonstrate that the CD8+ T cell immunogenicity of designed proteins can be tuned while preserving function, opening the door to incorporation of designed proteins in a next generation of adoptive cell therapies.

records.title: Generative design of functional disordered regions in a developmental transcription factor.
records.abstract: Rapid advances in protein structure design have not translated to intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). This is largely due to our incomplete understanding of how IDR sequence encodes function. Here, we use stem cell differentiation as a model to map functional sequence features in the C-terminal IDR of the transcription factor RUNX2, which is required to bind chromatin and regulate gene expression during osteogenesis. Surprisingly, linear IDR motifs are dispensable; instead, the conformational dynamics of the IDR predict function. We develop an algorithm for rational IDR design based on biophysical principles, and use it to generate functional IDRs de novo . These findings extend generative protein design beyond the folded proteome.

records.title: Janus nanoparticle-based electrochemical biosensors driven by the protein corona for tumour diagnosis: anisotropy as an analytical asset.
records.abstract: A Janus nanoparticle carries two chemically different faces on a single object of 10-500 nm. That broken symmetry lets a sensor do two things that compete for space on an isotropic particle: recognise an analyte on one face and transduce or amplify the recognition event on the other. The advantage is usually presented as geometric. It is not. In plasma, both faces are covered by a protein corona within seconds, and the corona not the engineered surface is what the analyte actually meets. Most of the biosensing literature treats this layer as contamination to be blocked. We argue instead that on an anisotropic particle the corona is a designable part of the interface, and that anisotropy is what makes it designable, because the two faces can be given different wettability, charge and curvature and therefore different coronas. This review examines that proposition in four steps. First, it sets out how Janus architectures are made and assembled on electrodes, and what the two faces contribute analytically. Second, it collects what is known about corona formation on nanoparticles and translates it into the variables a sensor designer can control, separating parameters with direct experimental support from those that are still inferred. Third, it examines how the corona changes charge transfer, mass transport and fouling at a modified electrode, and proposes three operating regimes corona-tolerant, corona-controlled and corona-exploitative with the analytical readout each one supports. Fourth, it compares what has been demonstrated in patient-derived samples with what remains projection. We conclude that the exploitative regime is coherent and testable, that no corona-driven Janus sensor has yet been validated prospectively in a clinical cohort, and that the immediate bottleneck is standardisation of the corona itself rather than ligand chemistry or electrode materials.

records.title: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma expressing human chorionic gonadotropin beta subunit.
records.abstract: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) is a high-grade, aggressive malignant tumour of fibrogenic origin, characterised by substantial cellular heterogeneity and poor prognosis. The lack of specific early clinical manifestations delays diagnosis and effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, we present a case of human chorionic gonadotropin beta subunit (hCGβ) expression in UPS. The presence of hCGβ was confirmed at both the mRNA and protein levels using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and immunohistochemistry, respectively. Transcripts encoding hCGβ were also detected in circulating tumour cells (CTCs) isolated from the patient's blood. These findings highlight hCGβ as a potential molecular marker associated with UPS biology and its tumour microenvironment. The identification of hCGβ-expressing CTCs through non-invasive liquid biopsy underscores the potential of this marker for real-time monitoring of tumour progression and for tailoring personalised therapeutic strategies. The results of the study support the growing concept that integrating molecular markers derived from the tumour microenvironment into diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks may significantly enhance precision oncology approaches for soft tissue sarcomas.

records.title: Clinical applications and recent advances in multimodal image fusion for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis: a narrative review.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and patient outcomes depend strongly on early detection, accurate staging, and timely treatment planning. However, single-modality imaging cannot fully characterize tumor heterogeneity because each modality provides only partial anatomical, functional, or metabolic information. Multimodal image fusion (MIF) addresses this limitation by integrating complementary data from ultrasound (US), computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET). This narrative review summarizes advances in MIF and its clinical applications in HCC. A targeted literature search of relevant databases was conducted, with a focus on recent and key English-language publications. The search strategy included terms related to "hepatocellular carcinoma", "CT", "MRI", "PET", "image registration", "image-guided ablation", and "artificial intelligence". This review summarizes commonly used image-fusion strategies and recent advances in their clinical applications for HCC, including lesion detection, staging, ablation guidance, and post-treatment assessment. It also discusses the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in image registration, fusion, and interpretation. MIF has shown clear clinical promise in supporting precision diagnosis and personalized management of HCC. Although MIF has shown clear clinical promise, its broader adoption remains limited by technical interoperability, cost, workflow complexity, and the need for standardized training. Future progress in system integration, algorithm robustness, and multidisciplinary collaboration may further expand its value in precision diagnosis and personalized management of HCC.

records.title: Adjuvant immunotherapy after curative-intent treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma: evidence, limitations, and a research framework for molecular residual disease-guided intervention-a narrative review.
records.abstract: Recurrence remains common after curative-intent treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), which are effective in advanced disease, have been evaluated empirically in patients with no radiologic evidence of tumor. The initial recurrence-free survival (RFS) advantage in IMbrave050 (NCT04102098) was not maintained with longer follow-up, and KEYNOTE-937 (NCT03867084) was negative. This review examines the limits of clinicopathologic risk selection and the potential role of molecular residual disease (MRD) in postoperative treatment decisions. PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, selected journal websites, and the American Society of Clinical Oncology and European Society for Medical Oncology meeting abstract repositories were searched for English-language reports from 1 January 2015 to 1 July 2026. Concepts included HCC, curative-intent treatment, adjuvant or perioperative immunotherapy, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), liquid biopsy, and MRD. Earlier landmark studies were traced from references. Guidelines, randomized trials, prospective cohorts, and translational studies were prioritized; non-HCC evidence was used only for methodology or trial design. Imaging-defined absence of tumor encompasses eradication of the index tumor, occult index-tumor-derived disease, and persistent liver-field risk for a new primary HCC. Clinicopathologic features estimate group-level recurrence risk but do not establish an individual's residual-disease state or ICI susceptibility. Updated IMbrave050 and reported KEYNOTE-937 results do not support routine empirical adjuvant ICI, although a phase II sintilimab trial reported benefit in patients with microvascular invasion. In CARES-009 (NCT04521153), resection was achieved in 92% versus 98%, and grade ≥ II surgical complications occurred in 35% versus 16%; the contribution of postoperative treatment cannot be isolated. Post-treatment ctDNA positivity is associated with poorer recurrence outcomes, but prediction of ICI benefit and utility of ctDNA-guided care remain unproven in randomized HCC trials. A nondetected result is informative only when input, assay quality, and baseline trackability are adequate. Future postoperative trials should integrate evidence of residual disease and treatment susceptibility with liver-related and treatment-related risks. Routine adjuvant ICI and treatment allocation based on MRD alone are not supported until biomarker-stratified randomized trials establish clinical utility.

records.title: Current imaging methods and molecular biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis: a narrative review.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one the seventh most prevalent form of cancer in the world and the third highest cause of cancer fatalities in different parts of the world, mostly due to the late diagnosis. and primarily associated with chronic liver diseases. HCC is heavily linked and associated with hepatitis B and C infections, as well as lifestyle factors such as heavy alcohol consumption, obesity, and diabetes. This narrative review critically evaluates current diagnostic approaches for HCC, including imaging modalities, liver biopsy, and established and emerging molecular biomarkers, while highlighting recent advances, existing limitations, and future diagnostic strategies. A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science to identify relevant English-language publications from 2009 to 2026. Original research articles, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical practice guidelines related to HCC diagnosis and surveillance were considered. The search terms covered HCC, imaging modalities, biomarkers, GALAD, GAAD, microRNA, and liquid biopsy. Guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD), the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL), and the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) were also reviewed. The reviewed evidence indicates that multiphasic computed tomography (CT) and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remain key imaging modalities for HCC diagnosis. Emerging biomarkers including des-γ-carboxy prothrombin (DCP), fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19), various microRNAs (miRNAs), and osteopontin (OPN), circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), show diagnostic potential, particularly when incorporated into multimarker panels or combined with conventional biomarkers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Artificial intelligence-assisted imaging and multimarker diagnostic models may also support earlier and more accurate detection. However, wider clinical implementation remains limited by insufficient multicentre validation, lack of assay standardization, limited reproducibility, and insufficient cost-effectiveness evidence. Modern diagnostic methods increasingly incorporate these imaging tools alongside molecular markers to yield a more accurate diagnosis and optimal treatment strategy. While liver biopsy remains the gold standard for histopathological confirmation, its invasive nature and associated risks highlight the urgent need for reliable, non-invasive diagnostic alternatives. This review provides insights into the current strategies to diagnose HCC and with an emphasis on innovative diagnostic strategies.
